about.title: Shasta Lake Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Shasta Lake is small enough that a death touches nearly everyone. With about 10,159 residents spread along Shasta Dam Boulevard, Cascade Boulevard and Wonderland Boulevard, the community tends to know when a family is grieving. Public records for 2025 list three injury collisions in the city and no traffic deaths, which is worth stating plainly: fatal crashes here are rare. Yet wrongful death claims in Shasta County arise from more than roadways. A fall at a rental property, a defective product, a workplace incident, or a collision on Rt 151 heading out of town can each leave a family facing funeral costs and a household income that has suddenly stopped. California law lets a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children bring a civil claim first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. The deadline is two years from the date of death, and shorter when a public agency is involved. LawProactive does not handle cases. We simply connect Shasta Lake families, for free, with an independent attorney who does, and who works on contingency.

items.question: Fatal crashes seem uncommon in Shasta Lake. Does a wrongful death claim still make sense here?
items.answer: Yes. The 2025 public record shows no traffic deaths within city limits, but wrongful death claims are not limited to roads. Deaths tied to unsafe property, a defective product, a workplace incident, or medical negligence can all qualify. An independent attorney can review what happened and explain whether a civil claim is realistic.

items.question: Is a wrongful death case the same as a criminal charge against the person responsible?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action brought by the family, and it proceeds separately from any criminal case the district attorney may or may not file. The civil case focuses on compensating the family's losses, not on punishment. One can move forward even when the other does not.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a death in Shasta County?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives families two years from the date of death. If a government entity may be responsible, such as a public agency tied to a roadway like Rt 151 or Shasta Dam Boulevard, the notice deadline is considerably shorter. Speaking with an attorney soon helps make sure no window closes while you are still grieving.
